item.title: Singularities and Collision Criteria in the Gravitational Straight-Segment Problem with Arbitrary Positive Density
item.description: arXiv:2611.08625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study singularities and collision criteria for a massless particle around a fixed finite straight segment with an arbitrary positive continuous density. We first show that every singularity forces the trajectory to approach the material segment. Using the axial symmetry of the potential, we prove that any trajectory approaching the segment is confined to an invariant plane containing it. Moreover, we show that every singularity is either a collision singularity or an ejection singularity. Finally, in the invariant plane, we introduce an angular-cone condition for positions and momenta directed toward the segment. We prove that if the initial position-momentum pair belongs to the angular cone, then the trajectory collides with the segment in finite time, and we derive an upper bound for the collision time. We further prove that the final arc of any collision satisfies the angular-cone condition.
item.dc:creator: F. Crespo, E. Mart\'{\i}nez, J. Vidarte, J. L. Zapata, A. Abdrabou

item.title: Stability of large dynamical systems using Gershgorin Disc Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.08692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the stability of large nonlinear dynamical systems is a fundamental problem in many fields, including biological, technological, and social networks. Traditional stability methods often rely on explicit eigenvalue calculations or the construction of Lyapunov functions, which become computationally difficult for large interconnected systems. In this work, we introduce a stability classifier that provides a computationally efficient way to determine the stability of complex systems without performing full spectral analysis. Our approach combines the Dynamical Jacobian Ensemble framework, which uses the network structure and the underlying dynamics to construct a Jacobian, with the Gershgorin disc theorem, which provides bounds on the eigenvalues of the system's Jacobian matrix. Using this combination, we derive an analytical classifier that predicts whether a dynamical system is asymptotically stable, unstable, or sensitively stable based on a small set of dynamical and network parameters. The analysis reveals that the stability of large dynamical systems is strongly influenced by highly connected hub nodes. This observation allows the stability condition to be simplified by focusing on the contribution of the hub-associated Gershgorin disc. Extensive numerical simulations on large ensembles of Jacobian matrices confirm that the proposed classifier accurately separates stable, unstable, and sensitively stable regimes across a wide range of dynamical parameters and network structures. The resulting framework provides a simple and scalable tool for predicting the stability of large dynamical networks while capturing the interplay between network topology and interaction dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Yuvrajsingh Pravinsingh Patil, Chandrakala Meena

item.title: Cantor's onion: a uniformly quasiregular map whose Julia set is a Cantor set of spheres
item.description: arXiv:2611.08773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integers $d,m\ge2$ with $1/d+1/m<1$, we construct a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{S}^3$ of degree $d^2+m^2$ whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components. The map is a three-dimensional analogue of McMullen's maps $z^d+\lambda/z^m$, built from two Zorich-type power maps glued across a single shell by a slit construction. Its Julia set has Hausdorff dimension $2+s$, where $d^{-s}+m^{-s}=1$, and the restriction of the map to its Julia set is a skew product over the shift on two symbols and has topological entropy $\log(d^2+m^2)$. We also prove that uniformly quasiregular maps that expand uniformly near their Julia set, possibly with branching there, have no wandering domains and only finitely many periodic Fatou components, all of them attracting basins. The map constructed here belongs to this class.
item.dc:creator: Alastair N. Fletcher, Gaven J. Martin

item.title: KAM theory for quasi-periodic equilibrium of generalized Frenkel-Kontorova model in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the KAM theory for one dimensional Frenkel-Kontorova model to multidimensional case in quasi-periodic media. By using the quasi-Newton method, we reduce the linearized operator with quasi-periodic coefficient in the Nash-Moser iteration to the composition of two diagonal operators and a near-identity operator, such that the small divisor problem can be overcome by imposing the simultaneous Diophantine condition. In contrast, we also discuss the application of Craig-Wayne-Bourgain method to the quasi-periodic equilibrium problem.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong He, Zuhong You

item.title: Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
item.description: arXiv:2611.08973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.
item.dc:creator: Be'eri Greenfeld, Paul-Henry Leemann, Carlos Gustavo Moreira, Efim Zelmanov

item.title: Asymptotic stability of high-index saddle dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.09049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) has been extensively adopted to compute saddle points of arbitrary index, with various applications such as constructing solution landscapes of complex systems. In this work, we prove the asymptotic stability of various HiSD methods, including the idealized, perturbed, and coupled HiSD methods, as well as their momentum-accelerated variants. The analysis is Jacobian-free and thus compensates for the linear stability analysis in the literature. The results not only provide specific characterizations for the convergence rate and the basin of attraction, but also reveal intrinsic correlations among dynamics in the coupled HiSD. Theoretical results are substantiated by numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Baoming Shi, Lei Zhang, Xiangcheng Zheng, Shangqin Zhu

item.title: Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations
item.description: arXiv:2611.09066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of $2$ and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman--Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems. When the affinity dimension is at most an explicit threshold determined by the Lyapunov exponents, the formula holds assuming only that there are no exact overlaps. Above the threshold, it holds under the strong open set condition. These dimension formulae are proved by approximation with finite diagonal subsystems. Assuming projective exponential separation, we also determine the pointwise dimensions of the coordinate projections of the equilibrium state. Below the threshold, the projections are not exact-dimensional: the pointwise dimension of each exists almost everywhere and takes exactly two values, each on a set of positive measure. At or above the threshold, both projections are exact-dimensional with dimension one.
item.dc:creator: Antti K\"aenm\"aki, R. D\'aniel Prokaj, K\'aroly Simon, Sascha Troscheit

item.title: Spectral Characterizations, Harmonic Analysis, and Phase Transitions in 2-Nice and $k$-Nice Recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2611.09143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structural mechanisms governing $2$-nice and $k$-nice recurrence in measure-preserving dynamical systems. For weakly mixing systems, we establish a complete spectral characterization of two-sided $2$-nice recurrence via quadratic spectral functionals and Herglotz--Bochner duality, extending the theory to arbitrary integer polynomial configurations $\{0, p_1(n), p_2(n)\}$ with zero constant term and to actions of countable abelian groups. Using stationary Gaussian processes and Hermite mode decoupling, we construct explicit weakly mixing counterexamples separating one-sided and two-sided $2$-nice recurrence. Furthermore, we uncover a fundamental structural phase transition at $k=3$: while $k=2$ recurrence is rigidly controlled by a quadratic spectral functional whose two-sided symmetrization eliminates all higher-degree cumulants, at $k=3$ fourth-order centered correlations survive symmetrization and can drive a strict recurrence deficit even when the quadratic spectral functional remains strictly positive. Using lacunary and multi-frequency Riesz products alongside uniform Wiener lemmas, we analyze the upper Banach density obstructions of negative spectral sets, establish partial partition regularity on the spectral cone, resolve an inverse Furstenberg correspondence problem of Rodr\'iguez Mart\'in for countable groups via Bernoulli product extensions, and characterize spectral $2$-nice ultrafilters in the Stone--\v{C}ech compactification $\beta\N$.
item.dc:creator: Dibyendu De

item.title: Hecke Algebras for Minimal Equicontinuous Cantor Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.09181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we extend the concept of Hecke algebras to a pair of a separable infinite profinite group and a closed core-free subgroup. Motivated by applications to minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions, which are characterized by such pairs, we characterize isometric *-algebra isomorphisms between such Hecke algebras by showing that they always arise as Koopman operators of homeomorphisms between the double coset spaces combined with the multiplication by some character. We then prove that two minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions with isometric isomorphic Hecke algebras have the same Steinitz order. We provide examples including the infinite dihedral group and the Grigorchuk group.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Lummerzheim

item.title: Unique ergodicity of systems of finite order and the density finite sums theorem in arbitrary abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.09333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a countable abelian group and $k\geq 1$. We establish that every minimal topological $\Gamma$-system of order $k$ is uniquely ergodic. This result, which was previously only known for finitely generated groups for arbitrary $k$, answers a question of Glasner, Gutman, and Ye and yields the answer to multiple questions by Candela, Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez, and Szegedy. As applications of our dynamical results, we obtain the following combinatorial theorems. Let $A\subseteq \Gamma$ be a set of positive upper Banach density. Then there are infinite sets $B_1,\ldots, B_k\subseteq \Gamma$ such that $B_1+\dots+B_k\subseteq A$. If $\Gamma$ satisfies a necessary divisibility assumption, then there are also $t\in \Gamma$ and an infinite set $B\subseteq \Gamma$ such that $A-t$ contains the set of all sums of $m$ pairwise distinct elements of $B$ for all $m\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$. For arbitrary $k$, these density finite sums theorems were only known in the integers previously.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Ackelsberg, Asgar Jamneshan, Or Shalom

item.title: On the existence of automorphisms acting expansively on the space of one-parameter subgroups of connected Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.09352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a connected Lie group $G$, we consider the action of Aut$(G)$ on Sub$_G$, the set of all closed subgroups of $G$ endowed with the Chabauty topology. We study the action of automorphisms of $G$ on Sub$^p_G$, the closure of the set of all closed one-parameter subgroups of $G$ in Sub$_G$, in terms of expansivity. We show that a nontrivial connected Lie group $G$ with dim$(G)\geq 2$ does not admit any automorphism which acts expansively on Sub$^p_G$. We also show that a certain class of subgroups of Aut$(G)$, which include all one-parameter groups of automorphisms in Aut$(G)$, do not act expansively on Sub$^p_G$. These results generalise a results of Chatterjee, Lekharu and Shah on tori and those of Prajapati and Shah on connected Lie groups of dimension greater than $1$.
item.dc:creator: Himanshu Lekharu, Riddhi Shah

item.title: Positivity of metric entropy of the standard map at large parameters
item.description: arXiv:2611.09361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the standard map $f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k\sin2\pi x,\,y+k\sin2\pi x)$ of the two-torus satisfies $\log(2\pi k+4)-2^{430}\le h_m(f_k)\le\log(2\pi k+4)$ for every $k\ge\exp(2^{50000})$, where $h_m$ is the metric entropy with respect to area. Thus $h_m(f_k)=\log k+O(1)$, the order of growth observed numerically since Chirikov; in particular $h_m(f_k)>0$ for all large $k$ and $h_m(f_k)\to\infty$, as conjectured by Sinai. Moreover, for each fixed $c<1$ the points whose top Lyapunov exponent is below $c\log k$ fill an area $O(1/\log k)$. Positivity of $h_m(f_k)$ for all sufficiently large $k$, with a threshold that is not effective, was obtained in a recent preprint by OpenAI. We keep some of its architecture and follow it closely in about a third of the results. New here are an explicit covering argument for cancellations and a balance across scales at a fixed parameter, an inequality between mean shortfalls that replaces the compactness argument over limits of rescaled orbit geometries; together they yield the explicit constants and the entropy bound.
item.dc:creator: S. Slijep\v{c}evi\'{c}

item.title: Every countable group has the nonsingular weak Rokhlin property
item.description: arXiv:2611.09453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every countable group $\Gamma$, in the space of nonsingular actions by $\Gamma$, there is an action whose orbit under conjugation is dense. This is the nonsingular analogue of the result of Glasner, Thouvenot, and Weiss that every countable group $\Gamma$ is weak Rokhlin, i.e., there is a dense orbit in the space of probability measure preserving $\Gamma$-actions.
item.dc:creator: Garrett Ervin, Bogl\'arka Geh\'er, Anett Imolay-Kocsis, M\'at\'e P\'alfy, Jenna Zomback

item.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $\lambda$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $\lambda \ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $\lambda \ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Matveev

item.title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
item.description: arXiv:2611.08591v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale $c$, with splitting $\Delta(c)\propto1/c$. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the $(4+\epsilon)$-dimensional $O(N)$ model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of $N$ through $N=4$ has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Behtash, Syo Kamata, Mauricio M. Martinez

item.title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $\mu$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-\'Elie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.
item.dc:creator: Richard Aoun, Sara Brofferio, Marc Peign\'e

item.title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.09034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $\mu \to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.
item.dc:creator: Lei Liu, Pedro A. S. Salom\~ao

item.title: Entropy and frame measures for self-similar measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.09190v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $0<\rho<1$ and a set of $N\ge2$ distinct real digits $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\mathbb{R}$, let \[ \mu_{\rho,\mathscr D}=\frac1N\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\mu_{\rho,\mathscr D}\circ S_i^{-1}, \qquad S_i(x)=\rho(x+d_i). \] Write $X=\sum_{j\ge1}\rho^j d_{\omega_j}$, where the symbols $\omega_j$ are independent and uniform on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. We prove that $\mu_{\rho,\mathscr D}$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy $H(\omega_1\mid X)>0$. In particular, this holds for all $\rho>1/N$, without any absolute-continuity assumption or arithmetic restriction on the digits or the contraction. At $\rho=1/N$, for commensurable digits, a frame measure exists if and only if $\mu_{\rho,\mathscr D}$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor. For $\mathscr D=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ and $\rho<1/N$, we also prove nonexistence whenever $\rho^{-m}=a/b$ for some $m\in\N$, with $a/b$ in lowest terms, $b\mid N$ and $N/b\nmid a$, extending the integer-power obstruction. The extension compares mask quotients using finite families of target pole classes in place of one target class.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyong Wang, Wei Tang

item.title: Synchronization transitions in Kuramoto oscillators with mixed interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.09564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic system for emergent synchronization phenomena, and significant efforts have been made to investigate its transition from incoherent to coherent dynamics. However, previous studies have almost exclusively assumed global coupling between the oscillators, even though many real-world systems are organized in specific network structures. Here, we fill this gap by examining finite-size effects in Kuramoto oscillator ensembles on networks with mixed-order interactions. Using numerical simulations, we show how parameters such as the size of the system, the average degree of the nodes and the strength of the interactions alter the behaviour of the transition to synchronization with respect to the known theoretical results that are derived for globally coupled infinite systems.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: A. Sharma, A. Suman, M. Anvari, M. Dev Shrimali, C. I. del Genio and S. Jalan, Eur. Phys. J. Spec. Top. 235, 7741 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Sharma, Ayushi Suman, Mehernaz Anvari, Manish Dev Shrimali, Charo I. del Genio, Sarika Jalan

item.title: Topological Mundici Adjunction and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.09608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a canonical topological lifting of Mundici equivalence, representing every topological MV-algebra as the unit interval of a topological $\ell$-group and extending the correspondence to a categorical adjunction. As applications, we give a direct group-theoretic proof of the equivalence of $T_0$ and $T_{3\frac12}$ and show that every topological MV-algebra is a retral space. We further extend the lifting to topological Riesz MV-algebras and identify the canonical topology with Wiweger's mixed topology under suitable assumptions, recovering the strict topology as a special case. Finally, we obtain a unit-interval formulation of Koopman representations for continuous-time dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Yanqiao Jia, Xueting Zhao, Yichuan Yang

item.title: Finite-Scale Folding and Maximal Asymptotic Variance
item.description: arXiv:2611.09697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: Pure mapping class group fixed points in $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify all the fixed points for the action of the pure mapping class group on $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$ character varieties of surface groups. Up to trivial peripheral monodromies, we prove that the irreducible fixed points are either pair of pants representations, or restrictions of reduced Burau representations to a once-punctured torus and restrictions of reduced Gassner representations to a 4-punctured sphere. On the other hand, we prove that the only non-trivial reducible fixed points appear in genus 0 where they map all but at most three peripheral loops in the centralizer of the image, and in genus 1 where they are valued in the quaternion group $H_8$. As consequences, we deduce (i) that an irreducible representation in genus 0 with at least four non-trivial peripheral monodromies is rigid if and only if it is a fixed point, and (ii) a partial classification of irreducible representations of pure braid groups into $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Bronstein, Thomas Le Fils, Arnaud Maret

item.title: Dense semigroups of triangular matrices
item.description: arXiv:1707.06293v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ be the semigroup of $n\times n$ lower triangular matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$. We show that $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ has dense subsemigroups generated by $n+1$ matrices, and that $n+1$ is the least possible number of generators; the same holds for dense subgroups of the group of invertible lower triangular matrices. The generators can be written down explicitly: $n$ of them are diagonal and one is a diagonal matrix plus a nilpotent perturbation. More precisely, let $D_0,\dots,D_m$ be diagonal matrices generating a dense subsemigroup of the diagonal matrices, where the diagonal entries of $D_0$ have strictly monotone moduli, and let $A$ be a lower triangular matrix with the same diagonal as $D_0$. We prove that the semigroup generated by $A,D_1,\dots,D_m$ is dense in $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ if and only if every subdiagonal entry of $A$ is nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Equivalence of synchronization states in the Kuramoto flow: a unified framework
item.description: arXiv:2503.19781v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On the fiftieth anniversary of the Kuramoto model, synchronization remains a central paradigm for collective behavior in complex oscillator systems. While phase locking, frequency synchronization, and order-parameter coherence are widely used to characterize synchronization, their precise dynamical relationship has remained unclear, especially in finite-dimensional systems beyond mean-field limits. In this work, we show that, in the fully connected Kuramoto model, full phase locking, phase locking, frequency synchronization, and order-parameter synchronization are dynamically equivalent. Moreover, we demonstrate that the equivalence between phase locking and frequency synchronization is governed by a topology-independent mechanism and persists for generic symmetric coupling structures. These results provide a unified dynamical framework for synchronization and clarify the structural role of the Kuramoto order parameter.
item.dc:creator: Ting-Yang Hsiao, Yun-Feng Lo, Chengbin Zhu

item.title: Phase diagram for intermittent maps
item.description: arXiv:2504.07864v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies the phase diagram of a fixed Pomeau--Manneville, or intermittent, map under a varying H\"older continuous potential of fixed exponent. Depending on the exponent, there are either one or two thermodynamic phases. The \emph{intermittent} phase is characterized by a unique Gibbs state whose typical orbits alternate irregularly between time intervals spent near the neutral fixed point and chaotic excursions away from it. The stationary phase is characterized by the Dirac mass at the neutral fixed point being the unique Gibbs state. Above a threshold exponent, every potential belongs to the intermittent phase, so the phase diagram is trivial. At or below the threshold, the phase transition locus is a co-dimension 1 topological submanifold separating the two phases, and it coincides with the set of potentials at which the pressure function fails to be real-analytic. This paper also investigates the relationships between the phase transition locus, (persistent) phase transitions in temperature, and ground states. It highlights a connection between phase transitions in temperature and ergodic optimization.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Coronel, Juan Rivera-Letelier

item.title: Multiple ergodic averages for commuting multiplicative actions
item.description: arXiv:2609.00405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the convergence of multiple ergodic averages involving several commuting multiplicative actions. We prove that for finitely generated systems, the averages $$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N S_{1,n}F_1\cdot\ldots\cdot S_{\ell,n}F_\ell$$ converge in norm, settling a conjecture of Frantzikinakis. Our proofs feature tools from ergodic theory and probabilistic number theory. We exploit some stability properties of additive functions to establish a novel variant of \Katai's orthogonality criterion, which leads to box seminorm control for our averages. Using the theory of magic extensions introduced by Host and a delicate complexity reduction argument, we eventually reduce our problem to known convergence results.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Charamaras, Andreas Koutsogiannis, Konstantinos Tsinas

item.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
item.description: arXiv:2609.28059v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$. Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.
item.dc:creator: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng

item.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.33287v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Abbondandolo, Pietro Majer

item.title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
item.description: arXiv:2611.03711v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum. We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_\sigma\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.
item.dc:creator: Penghui Wang, Xumin Wang, Rongwei Yang

item.title: The fixed-point proportion of Latt\`es maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.07816v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How often does an element of the geometric iterated Galois group of a Latt\`es map fix a vertex of the tree? Let A/K be an abelian variety over a separably closed field of characteristic 0, G <= Aut(A,0) finite, and alpha an isogeny of degree at least 2 normalising G. The Latt\`es map on X=A/G has a preimage tree governed by alpha-power torsion; we determine the fixed-point proportion in every dimension. For zeta in G the weight is the reciprocal of the number of fixed points of zeta in alpha-power torsion (zero if infinite); equivalently, it is a product of p-adic absolute values of determinants on the alpha-active subspaces; for scalar alpha=m the proportion is (1/|G|) times the sum over 1 != zeta in G of the product over p dividing m of the p-adic absolute value of det(1 - zeta | H_1(A,Z)). We deduce positivity and vanishing criteria, prove the groups G_infinity are martingale groups, determine the limit law, and reduce groups with translations to the fixed-origin case. In dimension one we determine ten values for scalar multipliers and nontrivial G <= Aut(E,0), and for the eight quadratic Latt\`es classes the proportions are 1/8, 1/4 and 5/16. Bridy-Jones-Kelsey-Lodge exclude the Latt\`es case from their main theorem; their Theorem 2.5 periodic-point bound is attained, via reductions modulo split primes p = 1 (mod 4), for the map (x^2+a)/(x^2-a), a^2 = -1, and we settle the exceptional case of the Fari\~na-Asategui-Radi conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Xin Li

item.title: Periodic solutions of symmetric Hamiltonian systems
item.description: arXiv:1906.02463v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of periodic solutions of Hamiltonian system $\dot z(t)=J \nabla H(z(t))$, where $H$ is symmetric under an action of a compact Lie group. We are looking for periodic solutions in a nearby of non-isolated critical points of $H$ which form orbits of the group action. We prove Lyapunov-type theorem for symmetric Hamiltonian systems.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Strzelecki

item.title: Convergence of optimizers implies eigenvalues filtering at equilibrium
item.description: arXiv:2510.09034v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ample empirical evidence in deep neural network training suggests that a variety of optimizers tend to find nearly global optima. In this article, we adopt the reversed perspective that convergence to an arbitrary point is assumed rather than proven, focusing on the consequences of this assumption. From this viewpoint, in line with recent advances on the edge-of-stability phenomenon, we argue that different optimizers effectively act as eigenvalue filters determined by their hyperparameters. Specifically, the standard gradient descent method inherently avoids the sharpest minima, whereas Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) algorithms go even further by actively favoring wider basins. Inspired by these insights, we propose two novel algorithms that exhibit enhanced eigenvalue filtering, effectively promoting wider minima. Our theoretical analysis leverages a generalized Hadamard--Perron stable manifold theorem and applies to general semialgebraic $C^2$ functions, without requiring additional non-degeneracy conditions or global Lipschitz bound assumptions. We support our conclusions with numerical experiments on feed-forward neural networks.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Transactions on Machine Learning Research 2025, 19 p
item.dc:creator: Jerome Bolte (TSE-R), Quoc-Tung Le (DAO), Edouard Pauwels (TSE-R)

item.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
item.description: arXiv:2601.03209v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain's proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is for example $1,2^{1/3},2^{-1/3}$. This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature $(2,2)$. The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature $(3,3)$ in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})^3\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^3$ over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner's measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.
item.dc:creator: Wooyeon Kim, Jens Marklof, Matthew Welsh

item.title: Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
item.description: arXiv:2602.00853v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1<p<2$ with $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-\delta})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $\delta>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Barrera, Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: Trajectory arclength reveals chaos
item.description: arXiv:2602.07660v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the time-averaged phase space arclength of a trajectory, expressed through a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, as a trajectory-based diagnostic for distinguishing regular and chaotic dynamics. The proposed indicator, $\Omega$, is computed by integrating the equations of motion together with a single scalar arclength-accumulation equation and therefore does not require variational equations, neighboring trajectories, or spatial derivatives of a Lagrangian descriptor field. Using Birkhoff's ergodic theorem together with estimates for quasiperiodic motion and correlation-based arguments for chaotic ergodic dynamics, we show that regular and chaotic trajectories exhibit different finite-time behavior despite the convergence of $\Omega$ in both regimes. For quasiperiodic trajectories with Diophantine frequency vectors, deviations from the limiting average decay as $\mathcal{O}(\tau^{-1})$, whereas sufficiently mixing chaotic dynamics exhibit root-mean-square fluctuations of order $\tau^{-1/2}$ under suitable correlation assumptions. This difference in finite-time convergence and fluctuation scaling provides the theoretical basis for using $\Omega$ to discriminate between the two dynamical regimes. We validate the proposed approach in the H\'enon--Heiles and Fermi--Pasta--Ulam systems, comparing the resulting classification of initial conditions with SALI as a reference chaos indicator. The results support $\Omega$ as a complementary single-trajectory diagnostic for chaos detection and as a practical source of scalar features for the analysis of trajectory ensembles, particularly in settings involving large numbers of trajectories or high-dimensional systems.
item.dc:creator: Javier Jim\'enez-L\'opez, V. J. Garc\'ia-Garrido

item.title: A family of matrix flows converging to normal matrices
item.description: arXiv:2602.11837v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The celebrated Antezana-Pujals-Stojanoff Theorem states that the iterated Aluthge transforms of an arbitrary matrix converge to a normal matrix. We introduce a family of matrix flows that share this convergence property by defining them through ordinary differential equations. The family includes a continuous analogue of the Aluthge transform, as well as a differential equation discussed by Haagerup in the context of II$_1$ factors. We also examine the same type of flows in the setting of Hilbert space operators equipped with unitarily invariant norms.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Izumi

item.title: Automatic feature identification in least-squares policy iteration using the Koopman operator framework
item.description: arXiv:2603.26464v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we present a Koopman autoencoder-based least-squares policy iteration (KAE-LSPI) algorithm for reinforcement learning (RL). The KAE-LSPI algorithm is based on reformulating the so-called least-squares fixed-point approximation method in terms of extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD), thereby enabling automatic feature learning via the Koopman autoencoder (KAE) framework. The approach is motivated by the lack of a systematic procedure for selecting features or kernels in linear RL techniques. Unlike previous approaches, no features or kernels need to be fixed a priori in our method. We discuss the theoretical convergence of KAE-LSPI under suitable assumptions, similar to kernel-based least-squares policy iteration (KLSPI). We empirically compare our method with two existing algorithms: least-squares policy iteration (LSPI) and KLSPI. In particular, for the chainwalk problem, the resulting policies are either optimal or nearly optimal for both three approaches. For the cart-pole system, KAE-LSPI outperforms the other two approaches in terms of policy performance.
item.dc:creator: Christian Mugisho Zagabe, Sebastian Peitz

item.title: Smooth Piecewise Cutting for Neural Operator to Handle Discontinuities and Sharp Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2605.19823v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural operators have achieved strong performance in learning solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs), but their inherently continuous representations struggle to capture discontinuities and sharp transitions. Existing approaches typically approximate such features within continuous function spaces, often requiring increased model capacity and high-resolution data. In this work, we propose Cut-DeepONet, a two-stage training framework that explicitly models discontinuities while reducing learning complexity. Our approach reformulates the problem via a lifting strategy, partitioning the domain into smooth subregions while representing discontinuities as boundaries in a higher-dimensional space. This separation aligns the operator learning task with the inductive bias of neural networks and avoids directly approximating discontinuities. An additional network predicts input-dependent discontinuity locations for unseen inputs, which are then used to guide the neural operator in generating smooth components within each region. Experiments on benchmark PDEs show that Cut-DeepONet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, even when trained on low-resolution datasets. The method excels on problems with discontinuities and sharp transitions, while using fewer trainable parameters. Our results highlight the benefits of changing the representation of operator learning rather than increasing model complexity.
item.dc:creator: Ha Dang, Sebastian Schmidt, Juergen Hesser

item.title: Robust Ensemble Kalman Filtering Under Observation Noise Misspecification
item.description: arXiv:2605.26881v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We address observation noise misspecification in Bayesian filtering of dynamical systems via generalised Bayesian inference. Mismatch in tail decay between the true data generating process and an assumed observation model, often indicated via outliers, can strongly impact Bayesian updates in Kalman filters and their ensemble approximations. Adjusting information processing in the analysis step by employing diffusion score matching achieves robustness while maintaining closed-form Gaussian updates and good uncertainty quantification. We provide theoretical properties of this novel Kalman filter in linear Gaussian state space systems covering conjugacy of the analysis step, robustness, covariance stability, and tuning. We extend the approach to non-linear signal dynamics by adapting ensemble Kalman filter variants. Simulation studies on 2D target tracking and the Lorenz-63 and 40D Lorenz-96 systems highlight a critical trade-off between robustness and stability in filtering.
item.dc:creator: Hans Reimann, Sebastian Reich

item.title: Mersenne Representation, the Conolly Sequence, and Soliton Profiles over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2607.22202v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the canonical skew-binary representation of nonnegative integers, whose positional weights are the Mersenne numbers \(2^{k}-1\), and its decomposition into the binary and nonbinary sides. The nonbinary values, arranged in increasing order, form the OEIS sequence A055938, and their successor structure gives a direct proof of the relation with the OEIS sequence A080578 that is recorded as conjectural in the OEIS entry for A080578. The resulting formulas show that the Conolly sequence describes both sides of the decomposition: a shifted Conolly sequence is the counting function of the binary side, while the same sequence gives the increasing enumeration of the nonbinary side. We then develop the parent map, truncation blocks, truncation remainders, and the Mersenne tau function associated with this representation. The parent map is conjugate to deletion of the lowest digit. Differences of the Mersenne tau rows recover the parent iterates and the counting function, and they give formulas for digit reconstruction and for a diagonal tau defect. Finally, we revisit a known finite-depth one-soliton family of the finite-field BBS. The Mersenne combinatorics is used directly to reconstruct a global integer-valued traveling-wave profile and to prove an integer window-counting theorem. Reduction modulo \(3\) yields the corresponding finite-field traveling-wave solutions. We also construct an integer-valued traveling-wave tau function whose front values are given by the Mersenne tau rows. The resulting construction shows how the combinatorics of a number representation can enter directly into the reconstruction of solutions of an integrable system.
item.dc:creator: Fumitaka Yura

item.title: Modular Existential Closedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.35409v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.
item.dc:creator: Vahagn Aslanyan
